title: There are few warnings in all of Scripture more terrifying than the words Jesus spoke in Matthew 7.
paragraphs: There are few warnings in all of Scripture more terrifying than the words Jesus spoke in Matthew 7.
Not because they were directed at atheists.
Not because they were spoken to pagans.
But because they were spoken to people who believed they belonged to Him.

People who said His name.
People who did ministry.
People who looked spiritually active.
People who convinced others they were saved.
And yet…
they were rejected.
Jesus said:

“Not every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven…”
— Matthew 7:21 (KJV)
The Greek text says:

Οὐ πᾶς ὁ λέγων μοι· Κύριε κύριε
(Ou pas ho legōn moi: Kyrie kyrie)
“Kýrie” means “Lord,” “Master,” or “Owner.”
This was not casual language.
These people acknowledged authority outwardly.
They verbally honored Jesus.
They confessed Him publicly.
And still…
He says many of them will never enter the Kingdom.
That should shake every person alive.
Because Jesus destroys one of the most dangerous lies in modern Christianity:
that verbal profession alone proves salvation.
Jesus continues:

“…but he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven.”
— Matthew 7:21
The phrase “doeth” comes from the Greek:
ποιῶν (poiōn)

It means:
to practice,
to carry out,
to live out continuously.
Jesus is not teaching salvation by works.
Scripture is crystal clear that salvation is by grace through faith:

“For by grace are ye saved through faith…”
— Ephesians 2:8
But the same passage continues:

“For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus unto good works…”
— Ephesians 2:10
True faith produces transformation.
Not perfection.
Transformation.
The problem in Matthew 7 is not that these people failed occasionally.
The problem is they built an entire spiritual identity disconnected from true obedience and relationship with Christ.
Listen carefully to what they say next:

“Many will say to me in that day, Lord, Lord, have we not prophesied in thy name? and in thy name have cast out devils? and in thy name done many wonderful works?”
— Matthew 7:22
Notice something horrifying.
They present their ministry résumé.
Their defense before a holy God is not repentance.
Not the mercy of Christ.
Not “Jesus saved me.”
Instead, it is:
“Look what I did.”
This is the religion of outward performance without inward surrender.
And Jesus answers with perhaps the most devastating sentence ever spoken:

“And then will I profess unto them, I never knew you: depart from me, ye that work iniquity.”
— Matthew 7:23
The Greek here is staggering.

οὐδέποτε ἔγνων ὑμᾶς
(oudepote egnōn hymas)
“I never knew you.”
The word “egnōn” comes from γινώσκω (ginōskō).
This is not intellectual awareness.
In Hebrew thought and biblical context, “to know” implies intimate relational covenant.
The Hebrew equivalent often reflects the word:
יָדַע (yada)

which means:
to know deeply,
personally,
intimately.
For example:

“And Adam knew Eve his wife…”
— Genesis 4:1
This was covenant intimacy.
So when Jesus says:
“I never knew you,”

He is not saying:
“I never heard of you.”
He is saying:
“You never belonged to Me in true covenant relationship.”
That changes everything.
Because modern Christianity often substitutes:

church attendance for surrender,
Christian content for holiness,
emotional experiences for repentance,
public ministry for private obedience.
A person can sing worship songs and still not know Christ.
A person can preach sermons and still not know Christ.
A person can build a massive ministry and still not know Christ.
Judas preached.
Judas cast out demons.
Judas walked with Jesus physically.
And Judas still belonged to destruction.
This is why Paul wrote:

“Examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith…”
— 2 Corinthians 13:5
Not everyone who feels spiritual is saved.
Not everyone who says “Lord” has surrendered to His Lordship.
The terrifying part is Jesus says:
“Many…”
Not few.
Many.
The Greek word is:
πολλοί (polloi)
A large number.
A multitude.
This warning is aimed directly at false assurance.
Especially religious deception.
Especially external Christianity without inward rebirth.
Jesus is confronting a heart that wants salvation without submission.
A crown without a cross.
Forgiveness without repentance.
Heaven without holiness.
But Scripture repeatedly teaches that true salvation changes a person.
Not instantly into perfection.
But directionally.

The heart begins to hate sin.
Conviction becomes real.
Repentance becomes ongoing.
The Holy Spirit begins transforming desires.
This is why 1 John says:

“He that saith, I know him, and keepeth not his commandments, is a liar…”
— 1 John 2:4
The Greek word for “keepeth” is:
τηρέω (tēreō)

Meaning:
to guard,
to preserve,
to observe carefully.
Again, this is not sinless perfection.
John himself acknowledged believers still sin:

“If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves…”
— 1 John 1:8
The issue is not whether Christians struggle.
The issue is whether someone lives in continual rebellion while claiming Christ.
Jesus never taught easy-believism.
He said:

“If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross daily, and follow me.”
— Luke 9:23
The Greek word for “deny” is:
ἀπαρνέομαι (aparneomai)

Meaning:
to utterly disown,
to renounce.
This is radical surrender.
And yet modern culture has created a version of Christianity where Jesus is treated like an accessory instead of King.
People want inspiration without crucifixion of the flesh.
People want blessings without obedience.
People want identity labels without transformation.
But Jesus sees beyond outward activity.
He sees the hidden life.
The secret compromises.
The unrepented sin.
The performance.
The masks.
The double life nobody else sees.
Hebrews says:

“All things are naked and opened unto the eyes of him with whom we have to do.”
— Hebrews 4:13
Nothing is hidden from Him.
Not the late-night addictions.
Not the hidden lust.
Not the bitterness.
Not the pride disguised as ministry.
Not the self-worship disguised as influence.
And still…
the invitation of grace remains open.
This warning from Jesus is not meant to drive broken repentant believers into despair.
It is meant to expose false assurance and awaken dead religion.
Peter denied Christ and was restored.
David fell horribly and was restored.
The prodigal son rebelled and was restored.
Why?
Because repentance was real.
The Hebrew concept of repentance is deeply connected to:
שׁוּב (shuv)

Meaning:
to return,
to turn back,
to come home again.
Biblical repentance is not mere guilt.
It is turning back to God.
And the beauty of the Gospel is this:
Jesus did not merely warn us.
He made a way for us.
At the cross, the wrath deserved by sinners was poured upon Christ.
The sinless One died for the guilty.
The righteous for the unrighteous.
And through His resurrection, forgiveness and reconciliation became available to all who truly repent and believe.
Not pretend belief.
Not cultural Christianity.
Not emotional moments.
Real surrender to the risen Christ.
This is why Jesus said in John 10:
“My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me.”

Again:
relationship and obedience.
Not performance and deception.
One of the most dangerous spiritual conditions is being close enough to Christian culture to feel safe while remaining far from Christ Himself.
You can know sermons and not know Jesus.
You can quote theology and not know Jesus.
You can defend doctrine online and not know Jesus.
You can appear morally clean publicly while rotting privately.
And one day…
every mask will come off.
Every platform will disappear.
Every audience will vanish.
Every hidden motive will be exposed before the throne of God.
And the only thing that will matter is this:
Did you truly belong to Jesus Christ?
Did you repent?
Did you trust Him?
Did your life reveal genuine transformation through the Holy Spirit?
Or did you simply build a religious identity around His name while never surrendering your heart?
That is why Jesus said:

“Enter ye in at the strait gate…”
— Matthew 7:13
Because the broad road is crowded with people who think they are safe.
But truth has never been determined by crowds.

The Gospel is not merely:
“Repeat these words.”

The Gospel is:
Christ crucified and risen,
calling sinners to repentance,
faith,
surrender,
and new life.
And the mercy of God is still available right now.
No matter how far someone has drifted.
No matter how fake they have been.
No matter how many hidden sins exist.
Christ still saves completely those who come to Him broken and repentant.
But Scripture leaves no room for comfortable hypocrisy.
Jesus is not merely Savior.
He is Lord.
And one day every knee will bow before Him.
The question is whether we bow now willingly in repentance…
or later in judgment.
If this message stirred conviction in you, don’t ignore it.
Draw near to Christ while there is still time.
Seek Him honestly.
Open the Scriptures.
Pray with sincerity instead of performance.
